rows.title: Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 names the review's sections and cards differently from today and puts each card straight under its numbered section heading, with no subsection heading above it. That also settles the repeated heading-then-card-title pairs DR1 parity row inc-147 left as an open design call (c-142). After this change the review reads '4. Uploaded documents' and '5. Consignment addresses', the cards are titled 'Origin of import', 'Main import reason', 'Additional details', 'Addresses' and 'Contact address', and each unfinished card's message follows its new title.
acceptanceCriteria: The review's fourth section heading reads '4. Uploaded documents' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-103; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-048; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-155)
The review's fifth section heading reads '5. Consignment addresses' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-108; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-048)

Every card stands directly under its numbered section heading: none of 'Where is this consignment coming from?', 'Main reason for import', 'Commodity details', 'Transit countries', 'Transport details', 'Upload documents', 'Roles and addresses' or 'Contact address for this consignment' appears as a heading, nor any other subsection heading above a card, and each card title is one heading level below its section heading (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-069, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-079, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-095; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-139; c-142)
The first card in '1. About the consignment' is titled 'Origin of import' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-070; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-157)

The import reason card is titled 'Main import reason' and its first row is keyed 'Main import reason' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-074; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-141)
The additional details card is titled 'Additional details' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-146)

'5. Consignment addresses' holds one card titled 'Addresses' whose single header Change link opens the roles and addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-151)

'6. Contact address' holds one card titled 'Contact address' with a 'Contact address' row, whose header Change link opens the contact address page and, on saving, returns to the review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-113; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-155, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-161)

An unfinished card's message, on the card and in the error summary, reads 'Complete origin of import' for Origin of import, 'Complete main import reason' for Main import reason and 'Complete additional details' for Additional details (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-046, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-048, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-050; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-082)
rows.gate: Look at the review's new heading structure (cards straight under numbered sections, card titles a level up) and the renamed cards: every later review row in this area builds its cards into this structure.
rows.notes: Pass 2 combines the heading, card-title and unfinished-message slices: each is one copy or heading change on the same review page with the same set-up and review, and the messages follow the card titles they name. Kept apart from the card-content rows so the structure lands once, first. The tests repo's view-state spec and page object find sections and cards by today's names ('4. Documents', 'Import details', 'Roles and addresses') and follow the new ones. Welsh copy keeps its existing shape.

rows.title: Review rows for origin, import reason, additional details and transport and arrival follow Design Release 2.1
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 changes which rows the About the consignment and Transport and arrival cards show and how they read. The region code row always shows, the 'required' row goes, a transit's exit point is the 'Exit border control post', the arrival date is 'at destination', means of transport read with the question's labels, transit countries move inside Arrival details with their own row Change link (settling the card-structure question DR1 parity row inc-146 left open, c-141), transit countries become optional for submission, every transporter row always shows, and an empty Additional details card is hidden.
acceptanceCriteria: The Origin of import card has no 'Region of origin code required' row (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-070; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-139)

The Origin of import card always shows a 'Region of origin code' row, reading 'Not applicable' when no code was needed (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-070, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-062)

For a Transit import the Main import reason card shows 'Exit border control post' and then 'Destination country', with no 'Port of exit' row (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-142)

The Additional details card shows only when it has a row to show, and has a Change link only when the additional details page is part of the notification's journey (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-091, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-094)
The Arrival details card labels the arrival date row 'Arrival date at destination' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-096; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-147)

The means of transport reads back with the label the means of transport question shows for the chosen option, for example 'Air' rather than 'Airplane' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-147)

When transit countries apply, they read back inside the Arrival details card under a 'Transit countries' subsection with the row 'Countries that the consignment will travel through', comma-separated in the order added, and that row has its own Change link to the transit countries page; there is no separate Transit countries card (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-098, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-148; c-141)

With transit countries in scope but none added, the review shows no 'Complete transit countries' message and no transit error, and Continue on an otherwise complete review goes on to the declaration (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-055, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-128)

The Transport details card always shows 'Name', 'Address', 'Country', 'Approval number' and 'Type', writing an empty answer as 'Not applicable', with Country read from the country stored on the transporter's address (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-100; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-149; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-010)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages' (card titles and heading levels). Pass 2 combines the About the consignment row slices (origin, import reason, additional details) with the Transport and arrival slices (arrival, transit, transporter): each is a row-level read-back change on review cards with the same set-up and review, and none carries an open question. Transit countries becoming optional for submission (req-880) changes what the review counts as unfinished; the transit countries page's own validation is the arrival-and-transit area's. c-review-and-submit-001 settled the transporter Country as the stored country.

rows.title: Review reads the commodity selection back in a 'What are you importing?' card and groups species under their commodity
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 reads the commodity selection back once, in its own card in section 1, and then shows one card per commodity in section 2 with a block per species, title-casing species names. Today each commodity line is its own card repeating code, common name and species. DR1 parity row inc-150 deferred how unfinished commodity and species answers are named; Design Release 2.1 supplies it (c-134), with links going to the card or block they were meant to reach.
acceptanceCriteria: '1. About the consignment' has a 'What are you importing?' card between Origin of import and Main import reason, with rows 'Commodity code', 'Common name' and 'Species' and a Change link to the commodity selection page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-069, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-071; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-139)

The What are you importing? card lists each selected commodity's code and name once, comma-separated, except 'other live mammals', where each species adds its own code and common name (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-072)

Species names on the review have every word capitalised, for example 'Bos Taurus', in the Species row and in each species block heading (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-073, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-081; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-158; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-050)

'2. Description of the goods' has one card per commodity titled '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)', holding one block per species headed with the species name, and the card's header Change link opens the consignment details page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-080, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-081; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-159, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-144)

A live-animal species block shows 'Number of animals' and no 'Commodity code', 'Common name' or 'Species' rows (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-082; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-144)
Where packaging applies to a species, its block shows 'Number of packages (when required)', reading 'Not applicable' when blank (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-082)

On an editable review the first row of each species block has its own Change link to the consignment details page, as well as the card's header Change link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-084)

With no commodity selected, the What are you importing? card is marked unfinished with 'Complete what are you importing?' and the error summary entry links to that card (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-047)

With the consignment details incomplete, the error summary shows 'Complete commodity details' linking to the first commodity card, and no commodity card is marked as an error card (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-049; c-134)
rows.gate: Look at the commodity card and species block layout, and where its row-level Change link sits: the germinal read-back and identification details rows build inside these blocks.
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages'. Pass 2 combines the new section 1 card, the commodity card and species block restructure, the species title-casing and the commodity-level unfinished messages: all reshape how the commodity selection reads back, on the same cards. Today's fit test pinning one Change link per card changes with the row-level link. The tests repo finds species cards by today's '<name> (<code>) — <species>' title and follows the new commodity card title.

rows.title: The germinal set's review reads germinal product answers back in their species blocks
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 reads a germinal product's total gross weight, package count, temperature and identification details back on the review. The 9 October ruling builds germinal products as their own set, each page a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, and keeps this row's germinal content for the germinal set's copy of the review. The germinal set always asks for temperature, takes weight as a decimal total gross weight in kilograms, and stores and shows its germinal details even where PIMS does not carry them.
acceptanceCriteria: In the germinal-products set's review, each species block shows 'Total gross weight' as '<n> kg', a decimal weight such as '12.5 kg' reading back as entered, and 'Number of packages' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-083; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-022)

In the germinal-products set's review, the first block of the first commodity card always shows a 'Temperature' row with the chosen answer (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-085; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021)

In the germinal-products set's review, a germinal species' identification details read back as a list of each identifier field and its saved value, including the details PIMS does not carry (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-087; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-042)
The live-animals set's review shows none of these germinal rows (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-110)
rows.notes: Re-drafted for the 9 October ruling: the germinal content of inc-105 is kept and built in the germinal set's copy of the review (claim 110), not in the live-animals review. Depends on the combiner's row that makes the germinal set's review copy (req-1843, germinal-products area), and on the germinal Commodity details row (keeps inc-017) and germinal identification row (inc-052's content), which let a germinal notification be answered. Depends on inc-104 because the germinal review is copied from the live review once it is built (claim 14). The germinal half of req-879 ('Enter the number of packages for <species>') was split out by claim 57 and is not here. This row's code now sits in the germinal set, so the combiner should consider moving it to the germinal-products theme (ruling claim 58).

rows.title: Identification details on the review: heading, animal labels, its own Change link and per-species unfinished messages
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads each species' identifier table 'Identification details', labels each animal by species and number, lets the trader change identifiers straight from the review, and, when more than one species is selected, names each species that is short of a count or an identifier. DR1 parity row inc-150 deferred the per-species marking for a design ruling; Design Release 2.1 supplies it (c-134).
acceptanceCriteria: A live-animal species block's identifier table is headed 'Identification details' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-159, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-145)

Each row of the table is labelled with the species name and the animal's number, for example 'Felis catus 1', under an 'Animal' column, with one column per identifier field (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-145)

On an editable review, Identification details has its own Change link opening the animal identification page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-145)

In the live-animals set, with more than one species selected and identifiers required, a species with no count is named 'Enter the number of animals for <species>', with the species name in lower case, and the error summary entry links to that species block (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-056, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-057, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-058; c-134)

With more than one species selected and identifiers required, a species with a count but no identifier is named 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <species>', with the species name in lower case, and the entry links to that species block (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-059, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-060; c-134)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Review reads the commodity selection back in a What are you importing? card…' (the species blocks the table and the error links sit in). Pass 2 combines the table copy, the Change link and the per-species unfinished messages: all are the identification part of a species block. req-879 is now the live-animals half only: the 9 October ruling (claim 57) split out the germinal 'Enter the number of packages for <species>' wording, which the germinal set's review builds. These messages are about a missing count or no identifier at all, so the one-identifier rule (claim 188) does not change them.

rows.title: Each uploaded document has its own card on the review, showing its file name
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 gives every uploaded document its own 'Document <n>' card with its own Change link, shows the attached file's name rather than its type, and shows a single 'Not applicable' card when nothing is uploaded. Today all documents share one card.
acceptanceCriteria: Each uploaded document has its own card in '4. Uploaded documents', titled 'Document <n>', whose header Change link opens the documents page, at the address it has today, and on saving returns to the review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-104, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-105; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-150, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-156)

Each document card shows 'Document reference', 'Document type', 'Date of issue' and 'Attachment', where Attachment is the uploaded file's name (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-104; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-150)

With no documents uploaded, '4. Uploaded documents' shows a single 'Document 1' card whose 'Document reference' reads 'Not applicable', and the words 'You have not added any documents yet.' no longer appear (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-106)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages' (section 4's name). Kept as its own row because it owns only the documents card and builds in parallel with the other card rows. The tests repo asserts today's empty-state sentence and follows the new card.

rows.title: Addresses card: permanent addresses, CPH format, one header link and a single unfinished entry
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows pets' permanent addresses in full in the Addresses card, writes the CPH with slashes, gives the Addresses and Contact address cards one header Change link and no row actions (c-138), returns a CPH change made from the review to the review (c-141, settling DR1 parity row inc-146's open question), and lists one error summary entry per unfinished card, so a deleted saved address is named once, on its card (c-135).
acceptanceCriteria: In the live-animals set, pets' permanent addresses read back in the Addresses card as a 'Permanent address' subsection, one entry per animal labelled '<common name> <n>' (for example 'Domestic cat 1') with the full address and 'United Kingdom', without email or phone, and the identification table has no Permanent address column (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-152, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-153)
The CPH number reads back with its parts separated by slashes, for example '12/345/6789' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-160, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-154)

No party row and no contact address row carries an 'Edit details' link: the Addresses and Contact address cards' header Change links are their only links (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-067; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-151; c-138)
A party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules still has an error summary entry linking to its edit page (c-138)

A trader who changes the CPH number from the Addresses card is returned to the review after saving, not sent onward through the journey (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-109, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-110; c-141)

When the consignor's saved address has been deleted, the error summary holds the single entry 'Complete roles and addresses' linking to the Addresses card, and 'Select an address for the consignor' shows on the consignor's row inside the card, with no separate consignor entry in the summary; the full error list for this case is pinned by a test (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-043; c-135)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages' (the Addresses and Contact address cards). Pass 2 combines the Addresses card's read-back slices (permanent addresses, CPH) with its link and error-summary slices (row actions, CPH return, deleted address): all change the same card and its errors. Moving the permanent address out of the identification table touches that table too; the identification row owns the table's other columns. The CPH page's own return behaviour may need the change context the CPH page reads (cph-permanent-and-contact area's page). The tests repo's page object clicks 'Edit details' today and follows the header link. req-848 is the live-animals set's only: the germinal set's review has no Permanent address subsection and no CPH row (req-1843, germinal-products area).

rows.title: Review ends with Continue and Delete, and an amendment's review offers Cancel amend and tells the trader they are re-submitting
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 ends an editable review with Continue and a red Delete. While amending, it adds a 'Cancel amend' button, retitles the review 'Review before re-submitting' once something has changed, and opens with no errors shown. The ruling's validation override still refuses an incomplete resubmission and says why (c-136). What the delete and cancel-amend confirmations do is the manage-notifications area's.
acceptanceCriteria: An editable journey or draft review ends with 'Continue' and, beside it, a red 'Delete' button that opens the notification's delete confirmation (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-115, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-118; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-162, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-157; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-084)

While a notification is being amended, the review ends with 'Continue', which submits, a secondary 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment confirmation, and a red 'Delete' button that opens the delete confirmation; there is no 'Cancel amendment' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-117; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-068, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-086)

An amendment's review is headed and titled 'Review your notification' when first opened, and 'Review before re-submitting' once any notification answer differs from the submitted version (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-019, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-082, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-083; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-064, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-065)

Changing only the uploaded documents during an amendment leaves the heading 'Review your notification', because only notification answers count as a change (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-084)
An amendment's review opens with no error summary and no card errors, even when answers are missing (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-040, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-041; c-136)
Pressing Continue on an amendment that is not complete does not submit it: the review is shown again with its error summary naming what is missing (c-136; ruling:sam-2026-10-07)
rows.notes: Pass 2 combines the review's end actions with the amendment review's heading and error behaviour: all are the review's own controls and state, with the same amend set-up. The backend already keeps a pre-amend snapshot of the notification separately from its documents; telling the frontend whether the notification answers differ from it is the backend part of this slice. The tests repo asserts today that a draft review has no Delete, and the cancel-amend spec uses the 'Cancel amendment' link; both follow. Delete and cancel-amend confirmations belong to manage-notifications; this row only links to them.

rows.title: A submitted notification's view has a header: reference, status, date submitted and a Back link to the overall dashboard
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads a submitted notification's view with its reference and status, dates it, and sends the trader back to the overall dashboard, which is the INS front door's (c-143, c-198). The 9 October ruling keys the header on the real route and the stored status, and keeps dashboard draft rows going to the hub, so the header shows for Submitted, Submitted action required and Completed, and a draft's review stays the journey review (c-246's default). The page title keeps the page name before the service, as accessibility requires (c-006). Opening the view of a notification that does not exist goes to the overall dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: A submitted notification's view shows its notification reference as the h1 in place of 'Review your notification', with its status beside it as a tag reading 'Submitted' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-020, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-179, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-173; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-067, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-090; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-096)

A submitted notification's view has the page title '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', while the journey review of a draft or an amendment keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-173; c-006)

Under the header, a submitted notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <d Month yyyy>', the date it was submitted (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-024; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-092; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-174)

On the workspace stack and in CDP, a submitted notification's view has a Back link to the overall dashboard in the INS front door (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-005, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-016; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-101; c-143; c-198; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-120)

A draft's review, reached from the hub's 'Review and submit', keeps the 'Review your notification' heading, the Draft status strip and the Back link to the hub, with no view header, no 'Date created' and no 'Import reference numbers' section (c-246 default; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-096, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-097; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-020)
Opening the view of a notification that does not exist goes to the overall dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-002, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-007; c-198)
rows.gate: Look at how the page tells a submitted notification's view from the journey review (keyed on the route and stored status), and at the view header: the header-actions, action-required and completed rows all build on this header.
openQuestions: c-246: with dashboard draft rows going to the hub, should a draft's review stay the journey review, or show the view header with the reference, 'Date created', 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and the Import reference numbers (req-900)? Default, which this row follows: a draft's review stays the journey review, and the header shows for Submitted, Submitted action required and Completed only.
rows.notes: Re-drafted for the 9 October ruling (claims 96 and 97): the header is keyed on the real route and the stored status, not on 'opened from the dashboard', so the draft content this row carried (req-900, the draft's 'Date created' and editable header view) is out; req-900 is now a question (c-246) and is not in this row. Pass 2 combines the view header (reference, status, title, date submitted) with its navigation (Back link, missing notification): one page state, one set-up. The backend already stores the submitted date but the view data carries only the created date; returning the submitted date is the backend part. The Back link and the missing-notification redirect use the animals frontend's configured INS front-door URL, which has a default; req-899's fallback to the set's own root when no INS URL is configured must be kept, but it is not written as a criterion because the setting always has a value in every environment this row runs in. Status tags for 'Submitted action required' and 'Submission complete'/'Completed' are the action-required and completed rows'. 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and 'Amend this notification' in the header are the header-actions row's.

rows.title: View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete, and shows the import reference numbers to copy
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 offers 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification, 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' on every submitted notification's view, and gives the trader the notification reference and customs document code they need for the customs declaration, each with a Copy button. Each state-changing control looks as Design Release 2.1 draws it but submits a form with the CSRF token (c-189). What amend, copy and delete do is the manage-notifications area's.
acceptanceCriteria: A Submitted notification's view header shows a primary 'Amend this notification' button, and a draft's review shows none (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-026; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-097)

A submitted notification's view header always offers 'Copy as new': a secondary button beside 'Amend this notification' when that shows, otherwise the primary button (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-098; c-189)

A submitted notification's view header always shows a red 'Delete' warning button that opens the notification's delete confirmation (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-029; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-017)

A submitted notification's view shows an 'Import reference numbers' section with the warning 'You must use the correct reference and code on the customs declaration or your consignment will be delayed.', a 'Notification reference' row with the reference and a 'Customs document code' row reading 'C640' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-035, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-036, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-037; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-093, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-094, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-096; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-180, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-176)

Each of the two import reference rows has its own secondary 'Copy' button, and pressing it puts that row's value on the clipboard (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-038, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-186; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-095; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-020 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-025)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'A submitted notification's view has a header…'. Pass 2 combines the header's three action buttons with the import reference numbers section: all sit in the view header under the same set-up. Following c-246's default, none of this shows on a draft's review: req-896 to req-898 now name the submitted statuses only. Amend and Copy as new submit forms (c-189); the actions themselves are the manage-notifications area's. The Copy buttons need JavaScript; without it the values stay visible as text to copy by hand. The Submitted action required and Completed states' buttons are checked in their own rows.

rows.title: Submitting records its date and outstanding items, and a notification still missing its health certificate shows as 'Submitted action required'
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 records the submission date and what is still outstanding at the declaration, and shows a notification submitted without its health certificate as 'Submitted action required': read-only, with a warning saying what to do, the missing certificate marked in section 4, and a Continue that leads back to the hub. The real service can only change a submitted notification through an amendment, so that Continue starts one (c-144). The identifier-driven items are a separate row.
acceptanceCriteria: After declaring and submitting, the notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <the day it was submitted>', and the same date on every later visit (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-145, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-155)

A notification submitted with no uploaded ITAHC or health certificate is shown from then on with the status tag 'Submitted action required'; one submitted with an ITAHC or health certificate shows 'Submitted' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-006, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-011; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-090)

The action-required view is read-only and its header carries a GOV.UK warning text reading 'You need to upload a health certificate' when the ITAHC is the only outstanding item (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-033, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-091)

On an action-required notification with no uploaded document, '4. Uploaded documents' shows the error 'Upload a valid health certificate' in place of document cards, inline, with no error summary (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-099)

The action-required view ends with 'Continue', which starts an amendment of the notification and opens its hub, where the trader can upload the certificate (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-120; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-041; c-144)

The action-required view header offers 'Amend this notification', 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' as a Submitted notification's does (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-027, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-029)
rows.notes: Depends on the rows 'A submitted notification's view has a header…' and 'View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete…'. Pass 2 combines recording the submission (date and outstanding items, req-909) with the action-required view it feeds: the view's status, warning and date come from the stored record, so neither is observable alone. How action-required is stored is the real team's design (9 October ruling, claim 98): the criteria name only what the trader sees. A re-submission from an amendment works the items out afresh. Uses the same ITAHC-or-health-certificate test as the confirmation page row (req-929). The dashboard flag for the same state is the 'Action required on the dashboard' row.

rows.title: Action required on the dashboard for a submitted notification missing its ITAHC
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 flags a submitted notification still missing its ITAHC on the dashboard cards. No real service records an 'Action required' status, so it is worked out in the animals backend from the notification's own record and carried into the INS read model (c-149), so that every dashboard listing the notification can show it.
acceptanceCriteria: On the live-animals notifications list, a submitted notification with no uploaded ITAHC or health certificate shows an 'Action required' tag on an error card, with a red marker hidden from assistive technology, and 'ITAHC is missing' as plain text under its reference (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-148, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-150, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-052, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-063, prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-064; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-046; c-149)

The INS front door's dashboard shows the same 'Action required' status and 'ITAHC is missing' for that notification, read from the INS read model (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p13-071; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-067, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-122; c-149)

A submitted notification with an ITAHC or health certificate uploaded shows no 'Action required' tag and no 'ITAHC is missing' text on either dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-148; c-149)

Once the missing certificate is uploaded through an amendment and the notification is re-submitted, both dashboards stop showing 'Action required' for it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-150; c-144; c-149)
rows.notes: Depends on the row 'Submitting records its date and outstanding items…' (the outstanding items the flag is worked out from). The combiner should merge or order this row with the notification-list area's 'Action required' card row and the dashboard-home area's Action needed rows: they build the same tag and the same read-model field. Where the notification-list area moves the live-animals list to the INS front door, the first criterion is observed there instead. How action-required is derived and stored is the real team's decision (c-149, ruling claim 98). 'Information is missing' for incomplete identifiers is the identifier row's.

rows.title: Declaration page: small checkbox in a hidden-legend fieldset, and no status strip
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1's declaration uses the small checkbox under a fieldset whose legend only screen readers hear, and shows no draft tag, reference or Cancel amend above its heading, at the end of a first submission and of an amendment alike.
acceptanceCriteria: The declaration confirmation is a GOV.UK small checkbox (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-139; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-169, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-163)

The checkbox sits in a fieldset whose legend 'Declaration confirmation' is announced by screen readers but not shown on screen (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-139; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-163)

The declaration page shows no status strip above its heading (no Draft, Amend or Amending tag, no notification reference and no Cancel amend), at the end of a first submission and of an amendment alike (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-170, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-077; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-077-m1)
rows.notes: Pass 2 keeps the three declaration slices together: same page, same set-up. Kept apart from the confirmation page row because they are separate feature folders that build in parallel. The tests repo's declaration page object and spec follow the hidden legend and the missing strip.

rows.title: Notification submitted page follows Design Release 2.1's guard, wording and links
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 guards the submitted (confirmation) page on the declaration, asks for the ITAHC by name and checks for one rather than for any document, tells the trader they can view or change the notification from the dashboard, sends 'Return to your dashboard' to the overall dashboard in the INS front door (c-143), and opens the HMRC links in a new tab.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening the confirmation page for a notification not yet submitted goes to the declaration page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-151; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-086)
The outstanding documents bullet reads 'upload the ITAHC and any other required documents' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-146)

The outstanding documents bullet shows when no uploaded document is an ITAHC or health certificate, even when other documents were uploaded, and does not show when one is (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-146)

The 'How to view or amend this notification' section reads 'You can view or change this notification from your dashboard.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-158; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-176; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-064)

On the workspace stack and in CDP, 'Return to your dashboard' goes to the overall dashboard in the INS front door (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-159; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-065; c-143)

The 'contact HMRC' and 'Find out about call charges' links open in a new tab, with the link text Design Release 2.1 gives them (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-164, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-165, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-166; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-178)
rows.notes: Pass 2 combines the confirmation page's guard, copy and link slices: one page, one set-up, no open question. req-935 ('Create a new notification') left this row: the 9 October ruling (claim 95, c-247) keeps today's real mechanism, so it is adopted as already met. The 'Return to your dashboard' link uses the animals frontend's configured INS front-door URL, which has a default; req-934's fallback to the set's own root when no INS URL is configured must be kept, but is not written as a criterion because the setting always has a value in every environment this row runs in. The ITAHC-or-health-certificate test should be the same one the submission record uses (req-909). The identifier bullet is the identifier row's.

rows.title: Template review: review your template before saving it
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 reviews a template on the review page before saving it: titled 'Review your template', with no errors, without uploaded documents or the arrival date, and ending with 'Save template'. Creating, listing and storing templates are the templates area's rows; this row is the review page's template variant.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Review template' opens the review page titled 'Review your template - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the h1 'Review your template' under the 'Template' caption and the template name, and it shows no error summary and no card errors (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-018, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-116; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-088; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-065)
The template review's main button reads 'Save template' and saves the template instead of going to the declaration (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-122)

The template review shows five sections, 'About the consignment', 'Description of the goods', 'Transport and arrival', '4. Consignment addresses' and '5. Contact address', with no uploaded documents section and no arrival date row, and reads 'Not applicable' for every unanswered row (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-097, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-103, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-108; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-090, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-091)

For a cattle template, the Additional details card has 'Certified for' and 'Includes unweaned animals', the Addresses card adds 'County parish holding (CPH) number', there is no identification details card, and 'Main import reason' holds a single row (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-112; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-090-m1)
rows.notes: Sits in inc-156 with the templates area's req-1336 and req-1338, which the combiner keeps there. Depends on the templates area's rows that create and store a template (there is no template in any service today), and on 'Review sections and cards take Design Release 2.1's headings, titles and unfinished-card messages'. The 9 October ruling (claims 103 and 104) names templates pages by page and section, never by path, and a template never offers documents or a declaration; the criteria follow both. backend is listed only where saving the template from the review needs the templates area's store.

rows.title: Template review ends with Save template and a Delete that discards or deletes the template
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 ends the template review with 'Save template' and a red Delete: for a template not yet saved it goes to the discard confirmation, which discards it, and for a saved template being edited to its delete confirmation, which deletes it.
acceptanceCriteria: The template review ends with 'Save template' and a red warning 'Delete' button that goes to the discard confirmation for a template not yet saved, which discards it, or to the template's delete confirmation for a saved template being edited, which deletes it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-119, prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-084; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-093; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-067; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-103)
rows.notes: Sits in inc-165 ('Delete a saved template') with the templates area's discard and delete requirements, which the combiner keeps there: the review's Delete is the way into those confirmations. req-943 is reworded by the 9 October ruling (claim 103) to name the confirmations by page, not by /templates/... path.

rows.title: Identifier-driven outstanding items: warnings, inline error, confirmation bullet and dashboard message
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 treats incomplete animal identifiers as an outstanding item: it names them in the action-required warnings, marks the species inline, adds a confirmation bullet and shows 'Information is missing' on the dashboard. The 9 October ruling closes DR1 inc-103 (one identifier is enough to identify an animal record) and removes this row's blocker (c-133). Identifiers are incomplete when a commodity line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified animal records than the animals it declares, which includes a single-species consignment with no identifier saved.
acceptanceCriteria: A notification that meets the submission minimum, but has a commodity line whose species asks for identifiers holding fewer identified animal records than the animals it declares, is submitted with the outstanding item 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification', shown on the confirmation page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-147; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-193; c-133)
A single-species consignment submitted with no identifier saved gets the same outstanding item on the confirmation page (c-133; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-147)

An animal record with one identifier filled counts as identified, so a notification whose every declared animal has a record with one identifier filled gets no identifier outstanding item (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-191)

An action-required notification missing both animal identifiers and its ITAHC shows the header warning 'You need to complete animal identifiers and upload a health certificate' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-031, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034)

An action-required notification missing only animal identifiers shows the header warning 'You need to complete animal identifiers' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-032, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034)

On an action-required notification, a species that needs identifiers but has none shows 'Identification details' with the inline error 'Enter a minimum of 1 identifier' in place of its content, inline with no error summary (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-090; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-042 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-045)
On the dashboard, a submitted notification with its ITAHC but incomplete identifiers shows the error 'Information is missing' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-149; c-149)
rows.notes: Unblocked by the 9 October ruling (claims 188 to 193): one identifier is enough, DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built, and inc-147's blocker is removed, so every requirement here is buildable now. Depends on 'Submitting records its date and outstanding items…' (inc-113), whose record of outstanding items this extends; on 'Action required on the dashboard…' (inc-131), whose read-model field carries the dashboard message; and on the identification details row (inc-106), the species block the inline error replaces. The same identified-record count decides submit and the hub's Complete status (claim 189); this row adds no stricter bar. The multi-line rule of inc-100 is written into the Behaviour Spec by that row (claim 194).

rows.title: A completed notification shows as complete with no Amend button
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a finished notification as 'Submission complete' (or its own status text, such as 'Completed') and stops amendment. No completed status reaches the real service today: post-submission outcomes come from the authorities' case system, which sends none back yet.
acceptanceCriteria: A completed notification's view shows the status tag 'Submission complete', or its own status text such as 'Completed' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-022; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-103; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-099)

A completed notification's view header has no 'Amend this notification' button, and still offers 'Copy as new' as the primary button and 'Delete' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-026, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-027, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-029)
openQuestions: A real source of completion must exist before the completed tag can show: no completed status reaches the service today, and the 9 October ruling (claim 99) names no provider. The likely one is the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sending post-submission outcomes back to the notification record (as req-1082). Until somebody names and builds that source, nothing here can be built or seen.
rows.notes: Blocked: req-910 carries blockedBy on a real source of completion (9 October ruling, claim 99). Once unblocked, it lands after the rows 'A submitted notification's view has a header…' and 'View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete…', and alongside whatever row builds that source.

rows.title: Tests prove the review, declaration and confirmation paths no test covers today
rows.detail: Today's suites leave several review, declaration and confirmation paths unproven, and many of them change in this programme. After this row each one has a test that fails if the behaviour breaks.
acceptanceCriteria: A test proves the review of a notification with several commodity lines reads back each commodity card and each species block with its rows (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-087)

A test proves the review's party address errors: a copied address that breaks the address-book rules and a deleted saved address each show their messages and links (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-071)

A test proves how the review shows a rejected document and a document still being scanned (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-088; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-067)

A test proves Cancel amend on the amendment review and each view header button (Amend this notification, Copy as new, Delete) leads where it should (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-101, trace-e2e-p13-105)

A test proves the confirmation page for a notification submitted with an ITAHC uploaded shows no outstanding documents item (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-063; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-057)

A test proves the declaration's refusal path: a ticked declaration on a notification the review refuses is not submitted and the trader is told why (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-059)

A test proves a failed submit and a stale submit (a notification changed or already submitted elsewhere) leave the notification unsubmitted and tell the trader (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-060)

A test proves a declaration ticked on an incomplete notification is refused and the trader is sent back to the review naming what is missing (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p14-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-087)
rows.notes: Depends on every todo row in this area whose behaviour it proves (commodity cards, Addresses card, documents cards, amendment review, view header actions, confirmation page), so each test asserts the Design Release 2.1 behaviour rather than today's. Each criterion is proved at whichever level fits (frontend fit spec or the tests repo's end-to-end suite); the planner picks. A failed or stale submit is driven through the backend's real refusal, mocked only at the network boundary in fit tests. The view header buttons are proved on a submitted notification, following c-246's default.
